DAY 109-111 — MAJOR CORRECTION: THE MOU WAS SIGNED 2 DAYS EARLY, AT VERSAILLES, NOT BURGENSTOCK. Wednesday June 17 evening: President Trump PERSONALLY SIGNED the US-Iran memorandum of understanding during a state dinner at the Palace of Versailles, France (G7 sidelines), with French President Macron standing beside him. IRAN'S PRESIDENT MASOUD PEZESHKIAN also signed in person — distinct from the earlier digital signing Sunday Jun 15 by VP Vance and Parliament Speaker Qalibaf. PAKISTAN PM SHEHBAZ SHARIF confirmed: 'Islamabad MoU shall enter into force with immediate effect and, as a first step, the Islamic Republic of Iran will instantly reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and the United States of America will immediately lift the naval blockade.' Sharif praised both Khamenei and Pezeshkian for 'wisdom, foresight and statesmanship.' THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION REVEALED THE 14-POINT MOU IN FULL Wednesday: (1) Immediate/permanent end to war on all fronts including Lebanon. (2) Mutual sovereignty respect, non-interference. (3) Hormuz: Iran's lead negotiator Ghalibaf said the strait 'will NOT return to pre-war conditions' — Iran will 'receive a fee for services' to shipping, meaning the PGSA toll framework persists in modified form. (4) Nuclear: Iran 'reaffirms it shall not procure or develop nuclear weapons'; enriched uranium to be 'down-blended on site under the supervision of the IAEA' via a mechanism still to be 'mutually agreed.' (5) $300 BILLION FUND DENIED: Trump — 'not investing 10 cents' — the deal instead permits THIRD-PARTY investment into Iran contingent on compliance, not a direct US fund (refuting earlier FT/Iranian-media reports). KHAMENEI AUTHORISED THE DEAL THURSDAY despite holding 'a different view,' after assurances from Pezeshkian that Iran's rights and 'Resistance Front' interests would be protected; Pezeshkian/SNSC pledged not to yield to 'excessive' future US demands. US LAWMAKERS (both parties) flagged concerns: nuclear verification mechanism undefined, Iran's missile programme not addressed. Trump will send the deal to Congress. IAEA DIRECTOR GROSSI: 'It is good that the memorandum is there. Now the technical work starts.' BURGENSTOCK TODAY (FRIDAY JUN 19): NOT a signing ceremony — Al Jazeera confirms documents 'already signed,' today is 'the official kickoff of the 59 days remaining for these sides to come to a conclusion.' Venue: Burgenstock Resort, Stansstad, near Lucerne, owned by Qatar's Katara Hospitality (same 2024 Ukraine peace summit venue). Vance + Ghalibaf attending. BRENT FRIDAY: $78.31 (-1.6%). WTI: $74.75 (-1.7%) — still above pre-war ~$70 given residual uncertainty on Hormuz administration mechanism and verification details. FOUR-DAY INDIA RALLY (through Wed Jun 17): Nifty +3.99% to 24,085.70 — first close above 24,000 since war. Sensex +4.50% to 77,155.62. VIX 13.18. US stock futures surged Wed evening on the surprise signing. West Asia War Day 111: THE WAR IS FORMALLY OVER; A 60-DAY FINAL-SETTLEMENT NEGOTIATION BEGINS TODAY.

THURSDAY MORNING: Trump threatened to hit Iran 'VERY HARD TONIGHT' and take 'TOTAL CONTROL' of Iran's oil and gas industries, including the Kharg Island export terminal (handles ~90% of Iran's oil exports) — Brent spiked to $93.5. THURSDAY AFTERNOON/EVENING: Trump abruptly CANCELLED the planned strikes via Truth Social: 'Based on the fact that discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran have been brought to the highest level of Iranian leadership and approved, I have, as President of the United States of America, cancelled the scheduled strikes.' Oval Office: 'We just made a great settlement of the war with Iran' — expects ceasefire-extension finalized 'over the next few days.' BUT IRAN'S RESPONSE WAS MIXED: FM spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said deal text 'mostly finalized' but 'contradictions in America's position has caused turbulence to this process.' A SENIOR IRANIAN OFFICIAL told MS NOW Iran has NOT YET agreed to any MOU or framework — directly contradicting Trump. SEPARATELY: UN Sec-Gen Guterres warned of risk of 'full war' — 'a lesser fire becoming full fire.' UN rights chief Turk: 'horrified... escalation upon escalation.' DAY 102-103. INDIA'S DARKEST DAY OF THE WAR. US NAVY STRUCK PALAU-FLAGGED TANKER MT SETTEBELLO in Gulf of Oman (intercepted June 9) — CENTCOM fired precision munitions into the engine room after crew 'repeatedly failed to comply with directions.' 3 OF 24 INDIAN SAILORS KILLED: Aditya Sharma (deck cadet), Shivanand Chaurashiya (engine fitter), Patnala Suresh (chief engineer) — FIRST DEATHS of US blockade since it began April 13. Remaining 21 Indians + 2 Pakistanis + 1 Russian + 1 Ukrainian evacuated by Omani Navy after engine fire/distress call. SECOND VESSEL MT JALVEER ATTACKED June 11 — all 20 Indians aboard safely evacuated — THIRD attack on a vessel with Indian sailors in 4 days. MEA SUMMONED US CHARGE D'AFFAIRES JASON MEEKS, handed formal demarche/protest. India to raise issue at G7 Evian-les-Bains (Jun 15-17) — PM Modi-Trump bilateral likely. Seamen Welfare Fund: ~Rs10 lakh compensation per deceased family. 562 Indian seafarers on 13 Indian-flagged vessels remain in Gulf (329 west of Hormuz, 233 Gulf of Oman); 18,000+ Indian seafarers total in region. military.t: JUL 7-9 MAJOR RE-ESCALATION: US Struck Iran 4 Times in 1 Week. Cyprus Ship Attacked. Iran Declared Hormuz 'Closed Until Further Notice' (CENTCOM Denied). US Revoked Iran Oil Export Licence. 80+ Iraq/Syria Sites Struck. Trump: 'Deal Is Over.'
military.d: Bloomberg, HDFC Sky, TradingEconomics (Jul 7-10): In the week of July 7-9 — overlapping with the end of Khamenei's funeral — the conflict re-escalated dramatically. An Iranian attack on a Cyprus-flagged container ship in the Strait of Hormuz triggered a US retaliation. The US carried out its fourth strike on Iran in a single week on Sunday July 9. Tehran declared the Strait of Hormuz would be 'closed until further notice,' a claim rejected by CENTCOM which said transit was proceeding. The US revoked Iran's oil export licence — a direct contradiction of the MOU's immediate sanctions waiver commitment, representing the most significant breach of the deal's terms yet. US forces also struck more than 80 Iranian-linked sites in Iraq and Syria. Trump declared the deal was 'over' though US officials simultaneously said technical talks were continuing. Iran's position: will not resume negotiations — particularly on nuclear issues — until the US fulfils prior commitments on Hormuz transit normalisation and oil export licensing. The dispute over MOU implementation (rather than the MOU terms themselves) is now the central obstacle.

military.t: JUN 19-22 BURGENSTOCK ROAD MAP: IAEA Inspectors Invited Back into Iran (Vance: 'Major Milestone'). Hormuz Deconfliction Channel + Demining Established. 3 Indian Tankers (860k MT) Crossed Hormuz. Roadmap for Final Deal Agreed.
military.d: Al Jazeera, NPR, Business Recorder (Jun 19-23): The Burgenstock talks (Jun 19-22) produced meaningful progress before the subsequent re-escalation. VP Vance described Iran agreeing to invite IAEA inspectors back as 'a major milestone for the American people and the first step in permanently denuclearising or permanently ending a nuclear weapons program in Iran.' A Hormuz deconfliction channel was established to 'avoid incidents and miscommunication with the aim of safe passage for commercial vessels,' and a demining coordination mechanism was set up. A Lebanon deconfliction cell was also agreed. Iran FM Araghchi summarised Iran's gains: oil and petrochemical export waivers, blockade lifted, some frozen assets released, reconstruction plan launched. India's Shipping Minister confirmed 3 Indian-flagged tankers carrying more than 860,000 metric tons of oil safely crossed the Strait of Hormuz — a direct positive outcome for India's energy supply chains.

Tuesday 8:45 AM IST. Day 136.

THE 72-HOUR COLLAPSE
• Jul 11 (Sat): Iran fired on a commercial ship in Hormuz and declared the strait closed completely. US struck back overnight — night 1.
• Jul 12 (Sun): Iran's widest Gulf barrage of the war — US bases in Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan and Oman; UAE under missile fire; Fujairah pumping stations hit. US night 2 hit dozens of targets with first combat use of one-way attack sea drones. UAE tankers Mombasa and Al Bahiyah struck in Omani waters — one Indian crew member killed, 6 Indians among 8 injured.
• Jul 13 (Mon): Trump reinstated 'The Iranian Blockade' plus tolls for Hormuz passage, effective Wed 1:30 AM IST, and notified Congress of resumed 'limited' military action. Night 3 began 2:15 AM IST Tuesday.

INDIA IMPACT
• 4th Indian war death; MEA response awaited. 562 seafarers on 13 Indian-flag vessels remain in the Gulf; Iran is demanding insurance fees and firing on non-compliant ships.
• Brent ~$79.8 — one-month high. OMC under-recovery re-widens; June trade deficit already at a 5-month high ($30.43B).
• GIFT Nifty 24,050 (-0.69%) signals a gap-down. Support 24,000 / 23,865. Rupee 95.65 with the 96 handle in play; VIX ~13.5 (+10%). IT remains the war hedge.

ASSESSMENT
• The MOU is wounded, not dead: Trump says a deal remains possible, the UN is pushing talks, and ~25 days remain to the ~Aug 16 expiry.
• Iran's play: make Hormuz unusable without its consent (fee-for-service), forcing Washington to concede tolls or escalate.
• US play: choke Iran's exports while keeping tolled third-party shipping moving and degrading Iran's anti-ship capability.
• Escalation test: whether US strikes stay 'limited' (the Congress-notification language) or extend to energy and leadership targets.

WATCHLIST — NEXT 72 HOURS
• Blockade start Wed 1:30 AM IST and Iran's response at sea.
• MEA statement on the Mombasa death; any DGS advisory for Indian seafarers; Op Urja Suraksha posture.
• Nifty 24,000 support; Brent $80.03 breakout level; rupee 96.
• Islamabad venue signals; Qatar mediation traffic.

CONFIDENCE
Market data verified across HDFC Sky, Business Standard, Sunday Guardian, TradingEconomics and Investing.com. Casualty details per UAE MoD statement. Strike details per CENTCOM and US officials — Iranian battle-damage claims unverified.
